memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: You may eat any clean bird. But these you may not eat: the eagle, the vulture, the black vulture, the red kite, the black kite, any kind of falcon, any kind of raven, the horned owl, the screech owl, the gull, any kind of hawk, the little owl, the great owl, the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey, the cormorant, the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe and the bat. All flying insects that swarm are unclean to you; do not eat them. But any winged creature that is clean you may eat. - Deut 14:11-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This long list of clean and unclean birds and insects can feel tedious to read, but it reveals something about God: He cares about details, and He calls His people to thoughtful discernment. Israel could not eat mindlessly; they had to know the difference, to distinguish, to choose carefully. Living as God's people required paying attention and exercising discernment in even the ordinary matter of food.

While these specific dietary rules no longer bind believers — for in Christ all foods are clean — the call to discernment endures and matters greatly. We live in a complex world full of choices, influences, ideas, and voices, not all of which are good for us. God calls His people to be discerning, to distinguish between what nourishes the soul and what harms it, to test things carefully rather than consuming whatever comes our way.

The New Testament urges this maturity: mature believers have "trained themselves to distinguish good from evil" (Heb 5:14). Discernment is a mark of spiritual growth. Just as Israel learned to distinguish clean from unclean, we are called to distinguish truth from error, wisdom from folly, what builds us up from what tears us down. This is not anxious legalism but wise, prayerful attentiveness. Ask God for discernment today — in what you read, watch, believe, and allow into your heart and mind. "Test everything; hold fast what is good" (1 Thess 5:21). A discerning heart is a protected heart.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Am I discerning about what I consume — ideas, influences, media?
- Do I test things carefully, or take in whatever comes my way?
- Where do I need God's discernment to distinguish good from harmful?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You call me to thoughtful discernment in a complex world. Give me wisdom to distinguish truth from error and what nourishes my soul from what harms it. Help me test everything and hold fast to what is good, guarding my heart and mind for You. Amen.
